correctness.rationale: The frozen construction is mathematically correct. Equality of B-pair sums first fixes the sum of group labels (the quadratic difference is smaller than L), then their product and unordered multiset. Quotient and remainder modulo R separate the physical choices within the groups, including a repeated group with its only distinct physical pair. Interleaving gives disjoint antipodal energy intervals. Inverse intensity DFT gives cyclic correlations; zero energy, no off-zero lags, two distinct off-zero lags, and the self-inverse lag are distinguished as in the proof. For nonantipodal support the magnitude ratio of one nonzero lag gives its unique amplitude product. Both two-site regimes solve the same nonsingular zero-lag system and then recover relative phase. The repaired proof retains these exact steps. For any positive amplitude budget the common exponential base exceeds one, so all orderings and product distinctions survive. With relative mask phase q/p=exp(iθ), the antipodal second real projection is cos(θ) Re(z) + sin(θ) Im(z) after normalization; together with Re(z) it is invertible exactly for sin(θ)≠0. When the alphabet is collinear, a common phase makes the mask real and the two signals e_0±i e_h have identical intensities at every frequency, though not phase-equivalent. Constant amplitude cannot locate a unit impulse even with varying phases; one mask alone cannot identify all impulses even with variable amplitudes. The recorded CHECK.py diagnostics apply to the quadrature specialization only; all alphabet and amplitude parameters in the repair follow from the analytic reconstruction, not from an executed or universal finite check.

originality.rationale: PASS for the repaired prescribed phase-alphabet criterion. The frozen headline claim of the unrestricted sharp two-pattern count is covered, not merely suspected: d1a29ce552bb states the same uniform two-sparse result for all even N≥2 using one flat and one bounded-contrast arbitrarily near-flat mask, and gives the same one-mask lower bound. That is an originality failure for the broad claim, not a correctness failure or a chronological priority determination. The substantive surviving result is that two prescribed phase settings suffice exactly when their ratio is nonreal, with arbitrary positive amplitude contrast. The matching near-flat theorem instead uses a distinct phase at every site and a phase-difference code for locating nonantipodal pairs. The repair replaces that freedom by amplitude-product coding combined with two phase settings, and credits the already known real-mask obstruction as its necessity half.
residual_risks: The matched almost-flat paper has the same catalogue date as the frozen original; no internal order or historical priority is inferred.

value.rationale: The repaired exact design addresses how many phase settings a single coded pattern actually requires beyond a flat pattern, while allowing amplitude variation. It gives an obstruction for any collinear alphabet and a matching construction from only two arbitrarily prescribed noncollinear settings, independent of the cycle length. This is materially useful when phase control is quantized: the support code no longer needs an individually resolved phase at every site. The theorem identifies which kind of second setting is necessary and sufficient, with positive amplitude contrast essential for locating impulses. It is not valued as a new count of patterns, or as a noise-stability guarantee.
